_note: I028: PC annotate batch A6 (library 0124-0127): menu graphics loaders, name entry, staff roll, text and dialogue renderers. Light depth for actors does not apply (no actor in this batch).

blockNote: Menu graphics and palette loaders (file offsets 74774-74832, SNES $02:A416-$A44F, bank 02).
=== MODEL ===

Two short routines give the field menus and the file-select screen their own BG2 tile set and colours. LoadMenuBg2Graphics DMAs graphics_04B000 ($09:B000, 8192 bytes, 256 4bpp tiles) to VRAM word $2000; LoadMenuPalette copies 256 bytes of data_04F000.binary_04F100 ($09:F100) into the CGRAM buffer (cgram_buffer, colours 0-127), which the NMI uploads.

Both are called in this order by OpenEquipmentMenu (lib_menus) and by lib_01232B (the setup of the file-select screen, called from EnterFileSelect). RedrawEquipmentPage (lib_menus) calls LoadMenuPalette alone to bring the equipment palette back after the item page.
=== NOTES ===

- VRAM word $2000 is the BG2 character base: lib_01232B writes BG12NBA = $20, BG2SC = $5C and BGMODE = 9 right before it calls these routines, and OpenEquipmentMenu writes the same BG2SC and BG12NBA. That graphics_04B000 is the menu icon and frame set and binary_04F100 its palette is a reading of the callers (OQ-I010-10).
- LoadMenuBg2Graphics does not write VMAIN ($2115); it relies on a value left by earlier code (OQ-I010-8) and on forced blank (both callers blank the screen first).
- The wrapper docs earlier called these code_012416 and code_01243D and the first one a '4 KB' set; the DMA size is $2000 bytes (8 KB, 4K words).

partNotes.LoadMenuBg2Graphics:
Loads the 8 KB menu tile set into VRAM at word address $2000.

When: OpenEquipmentMenu (X or Select in the field) and lib_01232B (setup of the file-select screen), with the screen blanked.
Sees: the frame, icon and gauge tiles that the BG2 menu page draws with (a reading of the callers, OQ-I010-10).
Why: the menus need their own character set; the scene's tiles are put back when the menu closes (RestoreSceneBgGfxAndPalette).
In: JSR; M = 8, X = 16; forced blank; VMAIN = $80 is assumed, not written here (OQ-I010-8).
Out: one DMA on channel 0 (mode 1, $2118/$2119): graphics_04B000 to VRAM word $2000, $2000 bytes.
Clobbers: A, X, DMA channel 0 registers.
partNotes.LoadMenuPalette:
Copies the 256-byte menu palette into the CGRAM buffer.

When: OpenEquipmentMenu, RedrawEquipmentPage (to restore the equipment colours after the item page) and lib_01232B.
Sees: the menu colours on the next NMI upload.
Why: the buffer is uploaded by the NMI, so loading the palette is a memory copy, not a hardware write.
In: JSR; M = 8, X = 16 (the routine switches to 16-bit A for the MVN and back to 8-bit).
Out: 256 bytes of binary_04F100 to cgram_buffer ($7F:0000, CGRAM colours 0-127); DBR and P restored.
Clobbers: A, X, Y.

74816.text: MVN with A = $FF: 256 bytes from $09:F100 to $7F:0000 (cgram_buffer)

blockNote: Name entry screen (file offsets 74990-75353 code, 83037-83222 strings; SNES $02:A4EE-$A658 and $02:C45D-$C515, bank 02).
=== MODEL ===

RunNameEntryScreen is one blocking routine: Cop3A_EnterPlayerName calls it once, at the start of the game after the Master's first speech (walkthrough 01-in-the-beginning.md: 'You will then get to pick a name for yourself. Choose what you will; there is no default name to be used'). The code agrees: the buffer is not pre-filled; it only continues a name that is already in it (the loop at loc_0124FF finds the first 0 byte).

The screen is plain BG3 text, drawn with PrintTextString from three strings: NameEntryFrameText (prompt, window, name line, placeholders), NameEntryGridText (the letter grid) and NameEntryCloseText (erases the window). Every change repaints both strings, which also erases the old cursor.
=== STATE ===
- X = BG3 byte offset of the cursor cell, from $03C6 (the blank cell left of 'A'); the letter is the tile at X + 2 (bg3_tilemap_buffer + 2 + X).
- name_cursor_col ($0441, 0-12) and name_cursor_row ($0443, 0-4); both are zeroed on entry.

- Y = write pointer into the name buffer $1B92-$1B99 (8 characters). A character is accepted while Y < $1B9A; the 0 terminator is stored at [Y] when the name is finished, so a full name has its terminator at $1B9A (OQ-I010-13).
=== GRID ===

13 columns, two tiles (4 bytes) per column, five rows: A-M, N-Z, a-m, n-z, then 0-9, '-', the tile $24 (printed by the extractor as an arrow: backspace) and the tile $23 (printed as AE: accept). Rows are $80 apart (one text row is two tile rows); an extra $40 follows rows 1 and 3, so Up and Down add or subtract $C0 there and Down from row 4 / Up from row 0 wrap by $280. Right from column 12 wraps by -$30, Left from column 0 by +$30.
=== BUTTONS (joy_pressed+1 bits) ===

Right (0) MoveNameCursorRight, Left (1) MoveNameCursorLeft, Down (2) MoveNameCursorDown, Up (3) MoveNameCursorUp, Start (4) FinishNameEntry (an empty name is ignored), Select (5) ignored, Y (6) DeleteNameChar (ignored when empty), B (7) PickNameChar (the tile under the letter decides: $23 finish, $24 backspace, else append with sound $18). Every cursor move jumps to BlipAndRedrawNameEntry (sound $07, then redraw). After each redraw the screen waits for all buttons to be released, so one press is one step.
=== NOTES ===
- Sound ids $07 and $18 are BRK requests (OQ-I010-16).
- The save-slot name copy at $0447-$044E (list entry 3 of TextListPointers) is filled by DrawSaveSlotMenu from the save block, not by this screen.
- FM-A6 correction: in NameEntryFrameText the [09] (one-row font) comes after the name [02:2], so only the placeholders are one-row; the name line is two-row.

partNotes.RunNameEntryScreen:
Runs the name entry screen until the player accepts a name, which is left in the name buffer.

When: Cop3A_EnterPlayerName, once, at the start of the game after the Master's first speech.
Sees: 'Please enter your name-', a 26 x 19 window with the letter grid, the name so far with eight + placeholders, and a cursor that the D-pad moves from letter to letter; B types the letter, Y deletes, Start finishes.
Why: one blocking routine owns the screen, so the COP script just continues when it returns.
In: long call (JSL); X = actor slot (Cop3A does TYX); M = 8, X = 16. Works with NMI on or off (WaitFrameReadButtons).
Out: name in $1B92-$1B99, 0-terminated at [Y]; returns after the close text and one frame. P, X and Y are restored.
Clobbers: A; name_cursor_col and name_cursor_row are zeroed.
partNotes.BlipAndRedrawNameEntry:
Plays the cursor sound, then redraws the screen with the cursor at its new cell.

When: after every cursor move and after a letter is typed (10 jumps).
Sees: a short click and the cursor jumping to the new letter.
Why: every move handler ends here, so the sound and the redraw are written once.
In: X = cursor cell, Y = name write pointer.
Out: BRK #$07, then falls into DrawNameEntryScreen.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.DrawNameEntryScreen:
Prints the frame text and the letter grid, draws the cursor and waits for the buttons to be released.

When: on entry and after every move, append and delete.
Sees: the whole screen repainted from the two strings (which erases the old cursor), then the cursor tile $2B in the cell and in the cell one row above (a two-row cursor).
Why: there is no dirty-cell logic: printing both strings is the redraw.
In: X = cursor cell, Y = name write pointer.
Out: NameEntryFrameText and NameEntryGridText printed with PrintTextString (X and Y kept); falls into the release wait (loc_012525: no key is read until joy_pressed+1 is 0) and then PollNameEntryKeys.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.PollNameEntryKeys:
Reads the pad once per frame and routes the pressed button to its handler.

When: the key loop of the name entry screen.
Sees: nothing by itself; the handlers do the visible work.
Why: a branch ladder over joy_pressed+1: bit 0 Right, 1 Left, 2 Down, 3 Up, 4 Start, 5 Select (skipped by a double LSR), 6 Y, 7 B; the first set bit wins.
In: -
Out: A = joy_pressed+1 from WaitFrameReadButtons; jumps to MoveNameCursorRight, MoveNameCursorLeft, MoveNameCursorDown, MoveNameCursorUp, FinishNameEntry, DeleteNameChar or PickNameChar; with no button (or Select) it loops.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.MoveNameCursorUp:
Moves the cursor up one grid row, wrapping from the top row to the bottom row.

When: the Up button in PollNameEntryKeys.
Sees: the cursor jumps to the letter above; from the first row it wraps to the digit row.
Why: the rows are not evenly spaced in the buffer (a blank row follows rows 1 and 3), so the step is computed.
In: name_cursor_row (0-4), X = cursor cell.
Out: row - 1 and X - $80 (X - $C0 when the old row was 2 or 4); from row 0: row 4 and X + $280. Jumps to BlipAndRedrawNameEntry.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.MoveNameCursorDown:
Moves the cursor down one grid row, wrapping from the bottom row to the top row.

When: the Down button in PollNameEntryKeys.
Sees: the cursor jumps to the letter below; from the digit row it wraps to the first row.
Why: same uneven row spacing as MoveNameCursorUp.
In: name_cursor_row (0-4), X = cursor cell.
Out: row + 1 and X + $80 (X + $C0 when the old row was 1 or 3); from row 4: row 0 and X - $280. Jumps to BlipAndRedrawNameEntry.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.MoveNameCursorLeft:
Moves the cursor one column left, wrapping from column 0 to column 12.

When: the Left button in PollNameEntryKeys.
Sees: the cursor jumps to the previous letter; from the first column it wraps to the last.
Why: a column is 4 bytes (two tiles), 13 columns, so the wrap is 12 * 4 = $30.
In: name_cursor_col (0-12), X = cursor cell.
Out: col - 1 and X - 4; from column 0: col 12 and X + $30. Jumps to BlipAndRedrawNameEntry.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.MoveNameCursorRight:
Moves the cursor one column right, wrapping from column 12 to column 0.

When: the Right button in PollNameEntryKeys.
Sees: the cursor jumps to the next letter; from the last column it wraps to the first.
Why: mirror of MoveNameCursorLeft.
In: name_cursor_col (0-12), X = cursor cell.
Out: col + 1 and X + 4; from column 12: col 0 and X - $30. Jumps to BlipAndRedrawNameEntry.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.DeleteNameChar:
Removes the last character of the name.

When: the Y button, or B on the backspace tile ($24).
Sees: the last typed letter disappears from the name line; nothing happens when the name is empty.
Why: the button and the grid tile share one routine.
In: Y = name write pointer.
Out: Y - 1 and 0 stored at [Y]; then BlipAndRedrawNameEntry. With Y = $1B92 (empty) it returns to PollNameEntryKeys without a redraw.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.PickNameChar:
Takes the grid cell under the cursor: a letter, the backspace tile or the accept tile.

When: the B button.
Sees: the letter is appended to the name line with the confirm sound; on the backspace tile the last letter is removed; on the accept tile the name is finished.
Why: the grid doubles as the control surface: tile $23 accepts and tile $24 deletes, so B needs no extra button.
In: X = cursor cell, Y = name write pointer.
Out: reads the tile at bg3_tilemap_buffer + 2 + X (the cell right of the cursor): $23 jumps to FinishNameEntry, $24 to DeleteNameChar; otherwise while Y < $1B9A the tile number is stored at [Y] and Y + 1 (loc_012631: BRK #$18, redraw); a ninth character is ignored (back to PollNameEntryKeys).
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.FinishNameEntry:
Ends the name entry: terminates the name and removes the window.

When: the Start button, or B on the accept tile.
Sees: the window disappears and the game goes on; an empty name is not accepted (nothing happens).
Why: the terminator goes where the buffer ended, so names shorter than 8 characters work.
In: Y = name write pointer.
Out: Y = $1B92 returns to PollNameEntryKeys; otherwise 0 is stored at [Y], NameEntryCloseText is printed (erases the window), one WaitFrameReadButtons frame runs and the routine returns (PLY, PLX, PLP, RTL: the exit of RunNameEntryScreen).
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.NameEntryFrameText:
Text of the name entry screen: prompt, window, name line and placeholders.

[CUR:184][07:1A,13] draws a window (26 wide, 19 high interior) at BG3 offset $184; [CUR:24A] prints 'Please enter your name-'; [CUR:318][02:2] prints the current name (list entry 2 = $1B92); [09] switches to the one-row font and [CUR:358] prints eight + placeholders. Printed by DrawNameEntryScreen.
partNotes.NameEntryGridText:
Text of the letter grid: [CUR:3C6] and then five rows of 13 columns, each column a blank followed by the letter (4 bytes per column).

Rows: A-M, N-Z, a-m, n-z, then 0-9, '-', the tile $24 (backspace) and the tile $23 (accept). [N][N] steps two tile rows ($80) between rows; after the second and fourth row [N][N][N] steps three ($C0). Printed by DrawNameEntryScreen; the cursor handlers rely on this spacing.
partNotes.NameEntryCloseText: Text that closes the name entry screen: [08:184] erases the window drawn at BG3 offset $184 (EraseWindowFrame). Printed by FinishNameEntry.

75001.text: Cursor starts on the blank cell left of 'A' ([CUR:3C6] of the grid); X = cursor cell from here on

75004.text: Y = name write pointer; the loop below moves it past a name already in the buffer

75035.text: Cursor tile $2B in the cell and in the cell one row above

75045.text: Release wait: no key is read until every button is up, so one press is one step

75052.text: A = joy_pressed+1; the LSR ladder tests Right, Left, Down, Up, Start, (Select skipped), Y, B

75116.text: Leaving row 2 or 4 upward: extra -$40 for the blank row after rows 1 and 3

75146.text: Wrap to row 4: +$280 = four row steps ($80, $C0, $80, $C0)

75234.text: Wrap to column 12: 12 columns x 4 bytes

75293.text: Tile right of the cursor = the letter: $23 accepts the name, $24 deletes, anything else is the character

75305.text: Accept only while Y < $1B9A: the name buffer is $1B92-$1B99 (8 characters)

75313.text: The tile number is the character code stored in the name

blockNote: Staff roll (credits) scroller (file offsets 75471-75625, SNES $02:A6CF-$A768, bank 02).
=== MODEL ===

ScrollStaffRollText prints a long string line by line on BG3 while scrolling the layer. The only caller is the credits actor of gv_front_end (code_007638, Y = gv_epilogue_texts.asciistring_016264, 'The staff of Soul Blazer ...'); afterwards the actor waits two COP 1B delays of $F0 frames and changes scene with COP 10. The walkthrough (08-world-of-evil.md) says only 'Enjoy the credits'; the credits text is not quoted there.

Each glyph is two tiles: tile c with attribute $21 (tile bit 8 set) at the write cell and tile c with attribute $20 one row below ((X + $40) & $7FF, wrapping inside the 2 KB page). [N] ($0D) scrolls scroll_bg3_y by 32 pixels, one pixel per RunSubFrame, moves the line start four tile rows down ((old + $100) & $7FF) and clears 128 words (four rows of tile 0, attribute $20) there. [14:n] moves the write cell right by n tiles. 0 ends.
The line start lives on the stack (one word, replaced on every [N]); the routine pops it at the end, so X is not preserved.
=== NOTES ===

- Whether the clear of the new line can overwrite a line still on screen, how long the roll runs and what the 8-bit scroll does when it wraps are open (OQ-I010-17, OQ-I010-12). Spelling oddities in the credits text are OQ-I010-11.

partNotes.ScrollStaffRollText:
Prints and scrolls the staff roll text, one line per 32 frames.

When: the credits actor of gv_front_end (code_007638), with Y = the credits string.
Sees: the credits (heading, names, copyright lines) scroll up the BG3 layer.
Why: the text is far longer than the 32-row BG3 page, so each line is written as the layer scrolls and the page rows that have scrolled away are reused.
In: long call (JSL); Y = string (bank $02); M = 8, X = 16; NMI off (RunSubFrame requires it, OQ-I005-20).
Out: the whole string printed and scrolled; P and DBR restored (DBR is forced to $02 inside). X is not preserved: it is popped from the line-start slot, so the caller saves it (code_007638 does PHX/PLX).
Clobbers: A, X, Y.
partNotes.NextStaffRollByte:
Fetches the next string byte and routes it; an ordinary byte is written as a two-tile glyph.

When: loop head of ScrollStaffRollText; every glyph, indent and line loops back here.
Sees: the letter appears at the write cell with its upper half one row above.
Why: one loop for the three codes (0, [N], [14:n]); anything else is a tile number.
In: Y = string pointer, X = write cell, line start on the stack.
Out: 0 goes to EndStaffRoll, $0D to ScrollStaffRollLine, $14 to IndentStaffRollLine; any other byte c is written as tile c with attribute $21 at X and tile c with attribute $20 at (X + $40) & $7FF, then X + 2.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.ScrollStaffRollLine:
Starts the next credits line: scrolls BG3 by four tile rows and clears the rows that scrolled in.

When: a [N] byte in the credits string.
Sees: the text moves up 32 pixels in 32 frames; the next line appears below the last one.
Why: the scroll is the animation, one pixel per frame; the clear prepares the page rows for the next line.
In: the line start is on the stack; X = write cell.
Out: vram_upload_flags bit 0 set; scroll_bg3_y + 32 with one RunSubFrame per pixel; new line start (old + $100) & $7FF replaces the stacked one; 128 words (tile 0, attribute $20) cleared from it; X = new line start.
Clobbers: A, dp$0C.
partNotes.IndentStaffRollLine:
Moves the write cell right by n tiles.

When: a [14:n] byte (the credits strings use 3 to 9).
Sees: names are indented under their headings.
Why: the credits layout is drawn with spaces that cost no string bytes.
In: Y at the operand byte n, X = write cell.
Out: X + 2n; Y + 1. The stacked line start is unchanged.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.EndStaffRoll:
Leaves ScrollStaffRollText.

When: the 0 terminator of the credits string.
Sees: the credits stop scrolling.
Why: the single exit of the routine.
Out: PLX (pops the line-start slot, so X = the last line start), PLB, PLP, RTL.

75479.text: First line start: BG3 row 28, column 1

75506.text: Top half: tile c with attribute $21 (bit 0 = tile bit 8, tile c + $100); the bottom half below uses $20

75516.text: Next row (+$40); the AND wraps inside the 2 KB page

75548.text: One pixel of scroll per sub-frame; 32 frames = four tile rows = one line

75562.text: New line start: four tile rows down

75573.text: Clear 128 words = the four 32-tile rows of the new line

blockNote: Text renderer and dialogue renderer for the BG3 page, with their helpers and the frame and button wait helpers (file offsets 75625-78198, SNES $02:A769-$B175; list strings at 83849-83906, SNES $02:C789-$C7C1; bank 02).
=== MODEL ===

Both renderers write tile words into the BG3 tile page bg3_tilemap_buffer ($7F7000, 32 x 32 tiles, 2 bytes per tile, row stride $40); the NMI uploads the page when vram_upload_flags bit 0 is set (DmaBg3TilemapPage) and every renderer sets that bit before it returns. Offsets are byte offsets into the page; [CUR:o] gives the offset, so a text row is $40 bytes and a column is 2.
A tile word is tile (low byte) and attribute (high byte): bits 0-1 are tile bits 8-9, bits 2-4 the palette, bit 5 priority. text_attr ($03E9) starts at $20 (priority, palette 0, tile bits 0).

Two-row glyphs: the default font draws a character c as two tiles, the lower half tile c at X and the upper half tile c + $100 (attribute + 1) one row up at X - $40, so a line occupies two rows and the first line of a window starts two rows below the origin. For the first page row the upper halves land in the 64 bytes before the page ($7F6FC0-$7F6FFF, OQ-I010-7). One-row mode ([09] toggles text_attr bit 1 = tile bit 9) writes only the lower tile; the HUD strings and the name-entry placeholders use it (OQ-I010-4). [0A] toggles text_font_flip bit 7, ORed into every tile low byte, selecting tiles $80-$FF (OQ-I010-3).

Strings live in bank $02 or in the WRAM mirror below $2000 (Y < $2000 reads WRAM: the player name $1B92, the debug buffer $1F02), because the renderers read them with DBR = $02. Bytes >= $80 are dictionary words: 12-byte entries of string_lookup_080000 (bank $10), expanded followed by one blank.
=== TWO RENDERERS ===

PrintTextString (menu renderer): prints at once, saves and restores text_attr and text_font_flip, forces DBR = $02, returns X = the last line start. 58 call sites: menus, status, HUD, gauges, title and file-select screens, name entry, Cop02 and Cop1A. No delay, no key wait, not resumable.

ShowDialogueText (dialogue renderer): typed text with a delay per glyph, key waits, paging and window scrolling, resumable. Callers: Cop01_ShowText, five sites in lib_tile_triggers_and_lair_return (chests and returns) and the debug scanner. It keeps the caller's DBR (bank $01 becomes $02), sets text_attr = $20, text_blip_flag = 1, text_font_flip = 0 and never restores text_attr and text_font_flip. It saves the line start in text_resume_pos at the end.
=== CONTROL CODES (operand widths as in us/stringTypes.json) ===
Code, operands, PrintTextString / ShowDialogueText:
- 00: none. End / wait for a key (WaitForButtonPress), then end.
- 01 [CUR:word]: X and the line start = word. Same in both.
- 02 [02:n] (byte): print TextListPointers[n] with PrintStringPlain / PrintDialogueString.
- 03 [03:v] (byte): text_attr = (text_attr & $E3) | v (replaces the palette bits; $24, $28, $2C = palette 1-3 with priority).
- 04 [04:a,b] (two words): the WORD ADDRESSES of the current and the maximum value (not the values); DrawGaugeBar (FM-A6 called them values).
- 05 [TBL:list,addr] (two words): list base and the WRAM address of the index; the entry is a pointer to the string.
- 06 [06:n,addr] (byte, word): n packed-BCD digits at addr, written right to left, leading zeros blanked except the last digit.

- 07 [07:w,h] (two bytes): window of w top-border tiles and h interior rows (DrawWindowFrame); the menu renderer also stores the origin in text_last_window_origin; the text cursor moves to line start + $82.
- 08 [08:origin] (word): erase the window at origin (EraseWindowFrame).
- 09: toggle one-row mode. 0A: toggle the alternate tile page.
- 0B [0B:tile,&count] (byte, word): repeat the tile 'count' times, count = the byte at the address (HudRepeatCounts). Menu renderer only; the dialogue renderer skips the three operand bytes.
- 0C [END]: ignored by the menu renderer; ends the dialogue without a key wait.
- 0D [N]: next line: line start + $40 (menu) / + $80 and scrolling at the bottom (dialogue).

- 0E [0E:n] delay n frames, 0F toggle the typing blip, 10 clear the window page and restart, 11 [FIN] blink the continue arrow, wait for B or Y, next line or restart page, 12 wait for a key: dialogue renderer only; the menu renderer prints these bytes as glyphs (OQ-I010-15).
- 13 [JMP:word]: continue the string at that address. 14 [14:n]: n blank cells (low tile bytes only; the attribute stays).
- 15-7F: glyph. 80-FF: dictionary word.
=== DIALOGUE BOX FLOW (ShowDialogueText) ===

1. First byte $10: the standard box [07:16,9] at offset $0408 (BG3 row 16, column 4; 22 x 9 interior) is drawn and the $10 is consumed. First byte $01: a plain print at the caller's X. Anything else: continue the previous dialogue at text_resume_pos (the next line when text_delay is not 0, otherwise a cleared page).

2. DispatchDialogueCode fetches bytes with ReadDialogueByte and dispatches; a glyph is written (PrintDialogueGlyph) and followed by TickAfterGlyph: it sets the upload bit, waits text_delay frames (WaitFrames, so actors keep running) and plays the blip (BRK #$07) while text_blip_flag is set; a blank does neither.

3. [N] (AdvanceDialogueLine): looks at the tile two rows below the line start. Not the bottom border (tile 4): next line, X + $80. Border: with text_delay 0 the page is prompted and restarted (PromptThenAdvance), otherwise the window interior scrolls up two rows (FindTextWindowBounds, ScrollTextWindowUp).

4. [FIN]: PromptThenAdvance measures the window, blinks the down arrow (tile $3D) under the line start (BlinkContinuePrompt: first while B or Y is still held, then until it is pressed), then goes to the next line (text_delay not 0) or restarts the page.
5. 00 (after a key wait) and [END] leave through EndDialogue: line start into text_resume_pos, upload bit set, P and DBR restored.

Window geometry written by FindTextWindowBounds: text_window_origin ($03EB, word) = interior top-left, text_window_width ($03ED) counted to tile 8, text_window_height ($03EF) counted to tile 6; the code reads the last two as words and relies on the high bytes being 0 (OQ-I010-9). Window tiles: 1 top-left, 2 top-right, 3 top, 4 bottom, 5 bottom-left, 6 bottom-right, 7 left, 8 right, $20 blank, $2B cursor, $3D continue arrow.
=== GAUGE BAR (DrawGaugeBar) ===

cur and max are read through the two addresses and only the low byte counts. The colour index is 2 * floor(cur / 10) taken before the clamp to 50 units, into data_00F9F7.word_00FB2F (13 words: dark blue for cur < 50, then lighter colours, white from 100); the colour goes to CGRAM colour 10 (HP bar of the HUD, bar start low byte $CC) or colour 14 (enemy bar). The bar is ceil(max / 2) tiles of $1B-$1F. This matches the walkthrough (level-up.md: 'fifty units in that bar ... each color adds ten more HP total, up to white'). A cur of 130 or more indexes past the table (OQ-I010-5).
=== WAIT HELPERS ===

WaitFrames (A frames of RunSubFrame), WaitForButtonPress (release, then press of B, Y or a direction), RunFrameReadButtons (one sub-frame, returns joy_pressed+1) and WaitFrameReadButtons (the same, or a vblank wait when NMI is on). They live in this file because the renderers use them.

text_attr $03E9 (byte); text_window_origin $03EB (word), text_window_width $03ED, text_window_height $03EF; text_resume_pos $03F3 (word; also written by the debug scanner); text_blip_flag $03F5 (bit 0, set to 1 at the start of a dialogue); text_last_window_origin $03F7 (word, origin of the last [07] drawn by the menu renderer; Cop02 and Cop1A erase it); text_font_flip $03F9 (bit 7); text_delay $1B84 (frames per printed glyph, 0 = instant; set to 3 by a new game, other values by speech scenes; the renderer reads a byte while the scenes write words, OQ-I010-1). The old reading of $1B84 as an ending flag is withdrawn.
=== DATA ===
TextListPointers ([02:n]) and its tile strings are at the end of the file.
=== NOTES ===
- Dictionary entry $06 is spelled 'Deathtole' in string_lookup_080000 while every dialogue spells 'Deathtoll' (OQ-I010-2, DISCREPANCY with the walkthrough; unchanged here).
- The helpers WaitFrames, RunFrameReadButtons and the dialogue renderer call RunSubFrame, so they need NMI off (OQ-I005-20).

partNotes.PrintTextString:
Prints a string into the BG3 tile page at once: the menu, status, HUD and gauge renderer.

When: 58 call sites in 10 files: Cop02 and Cop1A, the equipment, status and talk screens, the HUD, the title and file-select screens, the name entry screen, the pause screen and the front-end sequences.
Sees: the text appears on the next frame (the NMI uploads the page); no typing, no key wait.
Why: separate from ShowDialogueText because menus draw many strings in one frame and need no delay, waiting or paging.
In: long call (JSL); Y = string (bank $02 or WRAM below $2000); X = BG3 byte offset for strings that do not start with [CUR]; M = 8, X = 16.
Out: string printed, vram_upload_flags bit 0 set, DBR and P restored; X = the last line start; text_attr and text_font_flip restored to their values at entry.
Clobbers: A, X, Y; dp$00, $02, $0C, $0E, $0F.
Control codes: block note.
partNotes.DispatchTextCode:
Fetches the next string byte and routes it to its handler.

When: the loop head of PrintTextString; every handler and PrintGlyph jump back here.
Sees: -
Why: one dispatch for all control codes. $14 and $13 are tested first, then $0D, then any byte above $0D is a glyph (so $0E-$12 print as glyphs here), $00 ends, and a DEC ladder handles $01-$0B; $0C is ignored.
In: Y = string pointer, X = write cell, the line start on the stack.
Out: jumps to the handler of the code.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.PrintGlyph:
Writes one character as a two-tile glyph, or one tile in one-row mode.

When: any string byte $0E-$12 or $15-$7F.
Sees: the letter at the write cell with its upper half one row above.
Why: the font is two tiles tall: lower half tile c, upper half tile c + $100.
In: A = character, X = write cell; text_attr, text_font_flip.
Out: tile (c | text_font_flip) with attribute text_attr at X; unless text_attr bit 1 is set, tile c with attribute + 1 at X - $40; X + 2.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.HandleJumpCode:
[JMP:word]: continues the string at another address.

When: a $13 byte.
Sees: nothing; the text goes on from the other string.
Why: lets strings share a common tail.
In: Y at the 2-byte operand.
Out: Y = the word.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.HandleBlankRunCode:
[14:n]: writes n blank cells.

When: a $14 byte.
Sees: a gap in the line (menus use it for alignment).
Why: a run costs two string bytes instead of n spaces.
In: Y at the byte operand n, X = write cell.
Out: the tile low byte $20 stored n times; the attribute already on the page and the upper rows are left alone (text_font_flip is not applied); X + 2n; Y + 1.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.HandleRepeatTileCode:
[0B:tile,&count]: repeats a tile along the row.

When: a $0B byte (the HUD frame draws its bars with it).
Sees: a bar of identical tiles.
Why: the repeat count is a byte of ROM data (HudRepeatCounts) instead of part of the string.
In: Y at the operands: byte tile, word address of a byte holding the count.
Out: the word text_attr:tile written 'count' times from X (a count of 0 draws nothing); X advanced; Y after the operands.
Clobbers: A; dp$00.
partNotes.HandleAltFontCode:
[0A]: toggles the alternate tile page.

When: a $0A byte.
Sees: following characters use tiles $80-$FF (a 4 x 5 tile block of the title screen is drawn this way, asciistring_014176; the other uses are speech strings, OQ-I010-3).
Why: the flip is ORed into every tile low byte, so one flag changes the whole page of tiles.
In: -
Out: text_font_flip ^= $80.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.HandleFontPageCode:
[09]: toggles one-row mode.

When: a $09 byte.
Sees: following characters are one tile tall (HUD labels, the name entry placeholders).
Why: text_attr bit 1 is tile bit 9; the glyph code tests it to skip the upper half (OQ-I010-4).
In: -
Out: text_attr ^= $02.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.HandleEraseWindowCode:
[08:origin]: erases a window.

When: an $08 byte (NameEntryCloseText).
Sees: the window disappears.
Why: the string that closes a screen can remove its own window.
In: Y at the word operand.
Out: EraseWindowFrame at X = origin; X and the line start are unchanged; Y + 2.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.HandleWindowCode:
[07:w,h]: draws a window and starts the text inside it.

When: a $07 byte (menu and name entry windows).
Sees: a framed box.
Why: text and frame come from one string.
In: Y at the operands: byte w, byte h; X = origin.
Out: DrawWindowFrame; text_last_window_origin = X (Cop02 and Cop1A erase the choice window from it); the line start becomes line start + $82 (two rows and one tile in) and X follows.
Clobbers: A, X; dp$00, $02.
partNotes.HandleBcdNumberCode:
[06:n,addr]: prints an n-digit packed-BCD number.

When: a $06 byte (HP, level, gems, EXP).
Sees: the number with leading zeros blanked except the last digit.
Why: stats are kept as BCD so no binary-to-decimal routine is needed.
In: Y at the operands: byte n, word address of the BCD bytes (low nibble of the first byte is the last digit).
Out: digit tiles $30 + nibble written right to left from X + 2 * (n - 1); leading zeros replaced by $20; unless one-row mode is on, each digit's upper half is written one row up; X = the cell after the number.
Clobbers: A; dp$00, $02.
partNotes.HandleTableStringCode:
[TBL:list,addr]: prints entry i of a pointer list, i read from memory.

When: a $05 byte (item and magic names in the equipment window and the chest message).
Sees: the name of the item or spell whose id is in the WRAM cell.
Why: the string depends on game state, not on the script.
In: Y at the operands: word list base, word address of the index.
Out: PrintStringWithRuns on the pointer list[index].
Clobbers: A, X; dp$00.
partNotes.HandleGaugeCode:
[04:cur_addr,max_addr]: draws a gauge bar.

When: a $04 byte (the enemy bar of EnemyGaugeText, [04:336,338]).
Sees: a bar whose length and colour follow the two values.
Why: the string names the WRAM words, so the bar follows the game state.
In: Y at the operands: two word addresses (current value, maximum value).
Out: the two words read into dp$00 and dp$02, DrawGaugeBar; Y + 4.
Clobbers: A, X, Y; dp$00, $02.
partNotes.HandleAttributeCode:
[03:v]: sets the palette and priority bits.

When: a $03 byte.
Sees: following text in another palette (HUD colours).
Why: the attribute is part of the string, so no code is needed to recolour a label.
In: Y at the byte operand.
Out: text_attr = (text_attr & $E3) | v.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.HandleListStringCode:
[02:n]: prints list string n.

When: a $02 byte ([02:2] prints the player name in the status screen and many scripts).
Sees: the name or label.
Why: dynamic and shared strings (the player name at $1B92) live in one pointer list.
In: Y at the byte operand n.
Out: PrintStringPlain on TextListPointers[n]; Y + 1.
Clobbers: A, X.
partNotes.HandleCursorCode:
[CUR:word]: moves the write position.

When: a $01 byte (almost every string starts with one).
Sees: the text appears at that cell.
Why: placement is data in the string.
In: Y at the word operand.
Out: X = word and the stacked line start = word; Y + 2.
Clobbers: A, X.
partNotes.HandleNewlineCode:
[N]: next text row.

When: a $0D byte.
Sees: the following text starts one tile row ($40) below the line start (two-row glyphs need [N][N] for a full line).
Why: the line start is kept on the stack, so lines return to the same column.
In: stacked line start.
Out: line start + $40, X = line start.
Clobbers: A, X.
partNotes.EndTextString:
Finishes PrintTextString.

When: the 0 terminator.
Sees: the text appears on the next NMI upload.
Why: the single exit; it restores the state the caller had.
In: stack: line start, text_attr, text_font_flip, DBR, P.
Out: X = the last line start; text_attr and text_font_flip restored; vram_upload_flags bit 0 set; DBR and P restored; RTL.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.ReadTextByte:
Returns the next string byte for PrintTextString and expands dictionary words on the way.

When: the first step of every dispatch.
Sees: a dictionary word appears as its letters.
Why: the dictionary expansion draws the word and then reads on, so the dispatcher only ever sees ordinary bytes and control codes.
In: Y = string pointer.
Out: A = the next byte below $80, Y advanced; a byte of $80 or more is expanded by ExpandDictionaryWord first.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.ExpandDictionaryWord:
Prints dictionary word (byte & $7F) and one blank.

When: a string byte of $80 or more, in the menu renderer.
Sees: the word ('All', 'Soul', ...) in the current font, followed by a blank.
Why: dialogue and menu text repeat common words, so each is stored once in string_lookup_080000 (12-byte entries).
In: A = byte >= $80, X = write cell; the attribute in B.
Out: up to 12 characters of the entry (a 0 ends it early) written with the two-row or one-row rule, then one blank; X advanced; DBR restored; then back to ReadTextByte.
Clobbers: A, Y (saved); dp$0C.
partNotes.PrintStringWithRuns:
Prints a list string up to its 0 terminator, with [14:n] runs and dictionary words.

When: HandleTableStringCode (a pointer from a [TBL] list).
Sees: the item or spell name.
Why: list strings may contain blank runs, so they need the $14 case that PrintStringPlain lacks.
In: Y = string, X = write cell, the attribute in B (the caller did LDA text_attr, XBA).
Out: written to the 0 byte; Y on the terminator; X advanced.
Clobbers: A, X.
partNotes.PrintStringPlain:
Prints a list string up to its 0 terminator, without runs.

When: HandleListStringCode.
Sees: the player name, a HUD label.
Why: the list strings are fixed text, so no control codes are needed.
In: Y = string, X = write cell, the attribute in B.
Out: written to the 0 byte (dictionary words allowed); Y on the terminator; X advanced.
Clobbers: A, X.
partNotes.DrawGaugeBar:
Draws a gauge bar of up to 25 tiles and sets its colour.

When: the [04] code in both renderers (the HUD HP bar and the enemy bar).
Sees: a bar of 2 units per tile; its colour changes every 10 units (dark blue below 50, then lighter, white from 100).
Why: the HP can exceed the 50 units the bar can show, so the colour carries the tens above 50 (walkthrough level-up.md).
In: dp$00 = current, dp$02 = maximum (low bytes), X = bar start, M = 8.
Out: tiles $1B-$1F written (low bytes only); X = the cell after the bar; the colour word data_00F9F7.word_00FB2F[2 * floor(cur / 10)] stored in cgram_buffer colour 10 (bar start low byte $CC) or colour 14; cur and max clamped to 50 in dp$00 and dp$02.
Clobbers: A, X, Y; dp$00, $02. A cur of 130 or more reads past the 13-word table (OQ-I010-5).
partNotes.DrawWindowFrame:
Draws an empty window frame with a blank interior.

When: HandleWindowCode and DrawDialogueWindow.
Sees: a bordered box in the BG3 page.
Why: all windows share one frame layout whose border tiles other code recognizes (FindTextWindowBounds and EraseWindowFrame scan for them).
In: X = origin, dp$00 = width (top-border tiles), dp$02 = height (interior rows).
Out: tile 1 top-left, 3 top edge, 2 top-right; per row 7, interior words text_attr:$20, 8; then 5, 4 edge, 6 at the bottom. Rows are $40 apart.
Clobbers: A, X; dp$0C, $0E, $0F.
partNotes.EraseWindowFrame:
Erases a window frame, border and interior.

When: HandleEraseWindowCode and HandleDialogueEraseWindowCode, and Cop02 and Cop1A after a choice (the origin from text_last_window_origin).
Sees: the window disappears (the caller sets the upload bit).
Why: the window size is not stored, so the routine measures it from the border tiles.
In: long call (JSL); X = window origin, which must hold tile 1 (anything else is ignored).
Out: every row filled with tile 0, attribute $20 until the row ends in tile 6; vram_upload_flags is NOT set (both external callers set it).
Clobbers: A, X; Y preserved; dp$00, $01, $0C.
partNotes.ShowDialogueText:
Types a dialogue string into the BG3 page with a delay per glyph, key waits and paging.

When: Cop01_ShowText (every NPC line, sign and chest message), five sites in lib_tile_triggers_and_lair_return and the debug scanner.
Sees: the text window opens and the speech appears glyph by glyph; a down arrow blinks when the page is full and B or Y continues.
Why: separate from PrintTextString because dialogue needs the delay, the waits, the paging and the resume.
In: long call (JSL); Y = string; X = BG3 offset when the string starts with [CUR] (pushed as the line start; otherwise X is ignored and text_resume_pos is used); DBR = the caller's ($01 is changed to $02); M = 8, X = 16; NMI off.
Out: text typed, text_resume_pos saved at the end; P and DBR restored.
Clobbers: A, X, Y; text_attr, text_blip_flag and text_font_flip are initialised and not restored.
partNotes.InitDialogueState:
Initialises the text state and picks the entry path by the first string byte.

When: ShowDialogueText, right after the DBR choice.
Sees: -
Why: three ways in: open a box ($10), print at X ($01) or continue (anything else).
In: Y = string.
Out: text_attr = $20, text_blip_flag = 1, text_font_flip = 0; $01 goes to BeginPlainDialogue, $10 to OpenDialogueBox; otherwise X = text_resume_pos is pushed as the line start and the routine goes to AdvanceDialogueLine when text_delay is not 0, else to RestartDialoguePage.
Clobbers: A, X.
partNotes.OpenDialogueBox:
Draws the standard dialogue box.

When: a string whose first byte is $10.
Sees: a 22 x 9 box at BG3 row 16, column 4 (the lower part of the screen).
Why: most dialogues share the same box, so the first byte stands for [07:16,9] at $0408.
In: Y at the $10.
Out: the $10 is consumed; width $16 and height 9 set; falls through to DrawDialogueWindow with $0408 as the line start. text_last_window_origin is not set (OQ-I010-14).
Clobbers: A, X; dp$00, $02.
partNotes.BeginPlainDialogue:
Pushes the caller's X as the line start of a plain dialogue.

When: a string whose first byte is $01.
Sees: -
Why: the [CUR] code then replaces the pushed word, so X only matters for strings without it.
In: X = BG3 offset.
Out: X pushed; falls into DispatchDialogueCode.
partNotes.DispatchDialogueCode:
Fetches the next byte and routes it to its handler.

When: the loop head of ShowDialogueText; every handler jumps back here.
Sees: -
Why: the same ladder as DispatchTextCode with the dialogue-only codes $0E-$12 added and $0B skipped.
In: Y = string pointer, X = write cell, the line start on the stack.
Out: $0D to AdvanceDialogueLine, $14 to HandleDialogueBlankRun, bytes above $14 to PrintDialogueGlyph, $00 to HandleEndWaitCode, $01-$0C and $0E-$13 to their handlers.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.PrintDialogueGlyph:
Writes one character like PrintGlyph, then ticks.

When: any dialogue byte above $14.
Sees: the letter appears and the typing delay and blip follow.
Why: the dialogue version adds the tick and the one-row clean-up of the row above.
In: A = character, X = write cell.
Out: two-row write as PrintGlyph; in one-row mode a stale overlay tile above ($FE or $FF) is blanked and characters $CC-$F3 draw tile $FE and $F4 and above draw $FF in the row above (OQ-I010-6); TickAfterGlyph; X + 2.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.HandleDialogueJump:
[JMP:word] in dialogue: continues the string at another address.

When: a $13 byte.
Sees: nothing; the speech goes on from the other string.
Why: shared text tails.
In: Y at the word operand.
Out: Y = the word.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.HandleDialogueBlankRun:
[14:n] in dialogue: writes n blank cells with no tick.

When: a $14 byte.
Sees: an indent.
Why: same as HandleBlankRunCode without the typing delay.
In: Y at the byte operand, X = write cell.
Out: tile low byte $20 stored n times; X + 2n.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.HandleWaitKeyCode:
[12]: waits for a key.

When: a $12 byte.
Sees: the speech pauses until B, Y or a direction is pressed.
Why: lets a script split a line without a full page prompt.
In: -
Out: WaitForButtonPress.
Clobbers: A; joy_release_latch bits and joy_pressed+1 consumed.
partNotes.RestartDialoguePage:
Clears the box interior and restarts at its top.

When: the [10] code in a string, a continuation with text_delay 0, and PromptThenAdvance when text_delay is 0.
Sees: the box empties and the next text starts at the top line.
Why: a new page of speech replaces the old one.
In: the stacked line start (popped; any cell inside the window).
Out: FindTextWindowBounds, ClearTextWindowInterior; X = text_window_origin + $40 (second interior row: the first row takes the upper halves) and pushed as the line start.

partNotes.HandleBlipToggleCode:
[0F]: toggles the typing blip.

When: a $0F byte.
Sees: the per-glyph click turns off or on.
Why: some speech is silent.
In: -
Out: text_blip_flag ^= 1.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.HandleDelayCode:
[0E:n]: pauses the typing.

When: a $0E byte.
Sees: a pause of n frames in the speech (not with text_delay 0).
Why: dramatic pauses in scripted text.
In: Y at the byte operand n.
Out: WaitFrames(n) unless text_delay is 0; the operand is always consumed.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.SkipRepeatTileCode:
[0B] in dialogue: skips the three operand bytes; the repeat tile is not drawn.

When: a $0B byte in a dialogue string.
Sees: nothing.
Why: only the menu renderer draws repeats; the operands still have to be skipped.
In: Y at the operands.
Out: Y + 3.
partNotes.HandleDialogueAltFontCode:
[0A] in dialogue: toggles the alternate tile page, as HandleAltFontCode.

When: a $0A byte.
In: -
Out: text_font_flip ^= $80.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.HandleDialogueFontPageCode:
[09] in dialogue: toggles one-row mode, as HandleFontPageCode.

When: a $09 byte.
In: -
Out: text_attr ^= $02.

partNotes.HandleDialogueEraseWindowCode:
[08:origin] in dialogue: erases a window, as HandleEraseWindowCode.

When: an $08 byte.
In: Y at the word operand.
Out: EraseWindowFrame at X = origin; X restored; Y + 2.

[07:w,h] in dialogue: reads the size and falls into DrawDialogueWindow.

partNotes.HandleDialogueCursorCode:
[CUR:word] in dialogue: moves the write position, as HandleCursorCode.

partNotes.HandleFinishCode:
[FIN]: pulls the line start into X and prompts for a key.

partNotes.AdvanceDialogueLine:

partNotes.ScrollTextWindowUp:
Scrolls the window interior up by two rows and blanks the last two.

Why: lets long speech continue without a page prompt.
In: text_window_origin, text_window_width, text_window_height.
Out: height - 3 rows each copied from the row two below, then two rows filled with $2020; X preserved (PHX/PLX).
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.FindTextWindowBounds:
Measures the window around a cell and stores its geometry.

When: RestartDialoguePage, PromptThenAdvance and AdvanceDialogueLine.
Sees: -
Why: the window size is not stored when it is drawn, so the renderer scans the border tiles.
In: X = a cell inside the window.
Out: scans left to tile 7 and up to tile 3 (X = interior top-left, text_window_origin), right to tile 8 (text_window_width) and down to tile 6 (text_window_height); X and Y preserved.
Clobbers: A; dp$00.
partNotes.TickAfterGlyph:
Per-glyph pause and typing sound.

When: after every printed character of the dialogue renderer.
Sees: the speech appears at the speed set by text_delay, with a click per glyph.
Why: the single place for the typing speed.
In: A = the character.
Out: a blank ($20 or $A0) returns at once; otherwise vram_upload_flags bit 0 set, WaitFrames(text_delay), and BRK #$07 while text_blip_flag is not 0.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.WaitFrames:
Waits A frames by running RunSubFrame A times.

When: WaitReturnDone (A = $78), TryOpenChest, TickAfterGlyph and HandleDelayCode.
Sees: the game keeps running (actors animate) while the caller waits.
Why: a plain wait loop would freeze the actors.
In: long call (JSL); A = frames (M = 8); NMI off.
Out: returns after A sub-frames; A = 0.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.WaitForButtonPress:
Waits until no button is down, then until B, Y or a direction is pressed, and consumes the press.

When: [12] and the text end ($00) in dialogue.
Sees: the speech waits for the player.
Why: waiting for the release first stops a held button from skipping the page.
In: -
Out: B and Y latch bits cleared ($032B bits $C0) and joy_pressed+1 cleared; the mask $CF covers B, Y and the four directions.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.RunFrameReadButtons:
Runs one sub-frame and returns the pad state.

When: WaitForButtonPress, BlinkContinuePrompt and WaitFrameReadButtons.
Sees: one frame passes.
Why: the frame step for loops that must keep the game running with NMI off.
In: long call target of RunSubFrame; NMI off.
Out: A = joy_pressed+1 (B, Y, Select, Start, Up, Down, Left, Right from bit 7 to 0).
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.WaitFrameReadButtons:
Waits one frame in either NMI mode and returns the pad state.

When: the name entry screen, the row choosers and the menus.
Sees: one frame passes.
Why: the same menu code runs with NMI on and off.
In: JSR.
Out: NMI off (nmi_enabled = 0): RunFrameReadButtons; NMI on: WaitVBlank. A = joy_pressed+1.
Clobbers: A.
partNotes.TextListPointers:
List strings for the [02:n] text code: 9 pointers (index = n * 2).

00 ListHudBarLabelTiles and 01 ListEnemyBarLabelTiles (the six-tile labels of the HUD and enemy bars), 02 = $1B92 (the player name, a WRAM address: the strings are read through the low-RAM mirror), 03 = $0447 (the eight-byte name field that DrawSaveSlotMenu fills for a save slot line; no extracted ROM string uses [02:3]), 04-08 ListTileBlockRow1-5 (rows of a 4 x 5 tile block that gv_title_texts.asciistring_014176 draws). A mnemonic cannot name the WRAM entries: a name inside this pointer table changes the assembled bytes (I027).
partNotes.ListHudBarLabelTiles: Tiles $0A-$0F: the six-tile label printed by [02:0] in HudFrameText.
partNotes.ListEnemyBarLabelTiles: Tiles $10-$15: the six-tile label printed by [02:1] in EnemyGaugeText.
partNotes.ListTileBlockRow1: Tiles $0C-$0F: first of five rows of four tiles printed by [02:4]-[02:8] in gv_title_texts.asciistring_014176 (drawn with [09][0A], so the tile numbers get the alternate-page flip).
partNotes.ListTileBlockRow2: Tiles $1C-$1F: second row of the 4 x 5 tile block of ListTileBlockRow1.
partNotes.ListTileBlockRow3: Tiles $2C-$2F: third row of the 4 x 5 tile block of ListTileBlockRow1.
partNotes.ListTileBlockRow4: Tiles $3C-$3F: fourth row of the 4 x 5 tile block of ListTileBlockRow1.
partNotes.ListTileBlockRow5: Tiles $4C-$4F: fifth row of the 4 x 5 tile block of ListTileBlockRow1.

75633.text: Save the font flip and the attribute: EndTextString restores them

75641.text: Start every string with attribute $20 (priority, palette 0) and font flip 0

75680.text: Ladder: one DEC per code, $01-$0B; $0C falls through and is ignored

75748.text: Tile low byte = char | font flip ($80 = alternate tile page); attribute from text_attr

75765.text: text_attr bit 1 set = one-row mode: skip the upper half

75772.text: Upper half: attribute + 1 (tile bit 8) = tile c + $100, one row up (X was already advanced, hence the $7F6FBE base)

75817.text: Operands: byte tile, word address of a byte that holds the repeat count

75918.text: Remember the window origin: Cop02 and Cop1A erase the choice window from it

75928.text: First text cell: two rows and one tile in (the upper half of the first line needs the row above)

75948.text: X = last digit cell: start + 2 * (digits - 1); digits are written right to left

75978.text: Digit tile = $30 + nibble; the low nibble of the byte is the lower digit

76030.text: Leading zero: blank it; the last digit is never blanked (DEC of the count above)

76056.text: Upper half of the digit: same tile with tile bit 8, one row up

76083.text: Operands: word list base, word address of the index; the list entry is a string pointer

76125.text: Both operands are word ADDRESSES of the current and maximum value, not the values

76161.text: Replace the palette bits 2-4 and OR in v ($24, $28, $2C = palette 1-3 with priority)

76205.text: [CUR]: overwrite the stacked line start with the new offset

76266.text: x3 here, x4 below: 12 bytes per dictionary entry

76276.text: The dictionary is in bank $10: switch DBR

76305.text: Tile word bit 9 ($0200) = one-row mode: only the lower tile; else the upper half goes one row up

76326.text: One blank follows every dictionary word

76486.text: X = 2 * floor(cur / 10), taken before the clamp: index into the colour table

76496.text: Bar start low byte $CC = the HUD HP bar: colour 10 ($7F0014); any other bar uses colour 14 ($7F001C)

76536.text: Clamp cur (and max below) to 50 units

76555.text: Tiles: cur / 2 full ($1B), an odd unit ends in $1C or $1D, the rest empty ($1E), an odd max ends in $1F

76638.text: Frame tiles: 1 top-left, 3 top, 2 top-right, 7 left, 8 right, 5 bottom-left, 4 bottom, 6 bottom-right

76767.text: Only a window whose origin cell is tile 1 is erased

76843.text: $01,S = the caller's DBR (after PHP, PHB); bank $01 is switched to $02

76866.text: First byte: $01 = plain print at X, $10 = open the standard box, else continue the previous dialogue

76877.text: Continue: resume at the line start saved by the last call

76893.text: Standard box: BG3 row 16, column 4; 22 x 9 interior

76935.text: Same ladder as the menu renderer for $01-$0C; $0E-$13 follow below

77007.text: Two DECs: $0D was handled earlier, this reaches $0E

77080.text: One-row mode: blank a stale overlay tile above ($FE/$FF), then draw $FE (char $CC-$F3) or $FF ($F4+) above (OQ-I010-6)

77179.text: Line start = interior top-left + $40: the first interior row takes the upper halves

77200.text: text_delay 0 = instant text: the delay is skipped but the operand is still consumed

77599.text: Arrow column = (width - 1) & ~1 bytes from the line start, +$40 = the row below: centred under the text

77628.text: Tile two rows below the line start: tile 4 = bottom border = the box is full

77636.text: Box full: text_delay 0 prompts and restarts the page, otherwise the interior scrolls up two rows

77667.text: Remember the line start: a later call with another first byte continues here

77844.text: Height and width are words but are stored as bytes; the high bytes are assumed 0 (OQ-I010-9)

77900.text: Blink: shown while frame_counter bit 4 is set (16 frames on, 16 off); this loop runs while B or Y is still held, the one at loc_013069 waits for a press

77962.text: Rows copied = height - 3: each takes the row two below it; the last two rows are cleared

78028.text: Scan left for tile 7, up for tile 3 ($7F6FC0 = X - $40), right for tile 8, down for tile 6

78116.text: A blank ($20, or $A0 in the alternate font) neither waits nor clicks

78157.text: $CF = B, Y and the four directions

78168.text: Consume the B and Y latch bits so the press is not seen twice

78185.text: NMI off: drive one sub-frame; NMI on: wait for vblank

21425.text: text_delay = 6: frames per printed glyph from now on (a new game sets 3, lib_027912; OQ-I028-1)
